taxonomyNote: NatureServe includes two subspecies (A. m. mutica, A. m. calvata) and notes some field guides treat calvata as a full species; ADW titles the species 'Smooth Softshelled Turtle'.
fieldMarks: Medium-large softshell; female carapace 16.5-35.6 cm, males 11.5-26.6 cm; leathery, skin-covered oval carapace without spines on the front edge.
Olive to orange carapace with dark spots, streaks or blotches (females blotchier); plastron plain white or grey.
Cream or orange line bordered in black runs from behind each eye to the neck; tubular snout with round nostrils and no septal ridge.
Males have thicker tails than females.
behavior: Most aquatic of the North American softshells; buries in bottom sediment so only the snout reaches the surface, and overwinters buried underwater.
Emerges from hibernation in March or early April in Kansas; basks on sandbars and mudflats.
Carnivorous generalist eating insects, crayfish, snails, fish and amphibians.
habitat: Large rivers and streams, sometimes lakes, impoundments and shallow bogs, usually with sand or mud bottoms and little vegetation; nests on open sandbars and banks near water.
range: Native across the central and south-central US (NatureServe lists Pennsylvania, the Midwest and Great Plains south to Texas, New Mexico and Florida); introduced in France (ADW). Not recorded for Canada in NatureServe.
